questions.q: What are the four possible bottlenecks in a data flow run?
options: Cluster start-up time, reading from source, transformation time, and writing to sink
Parameters, variables, triggers, and datasets
Authoring, publishing, monitoring, and archiving
Linked services, datasets, pipelines, and activities
questions.explain: The monitoring view breaks execution into these four stages — finding which one is largest tells you where tuning effort will actually pay off.

questions.q: How should you decide where to focus performance tuning effort?
options: Find the largest bottleneck in the monitoring view first, rather than guessing
Always start by changing partitioning, regardless of what the monitor shows
Always increase the logging level to Verbose first
Tuning effort doesn't matter — every stage takes the same time
questions.explain: The monitoring view shows exactly which stage dominates run time — that's where to focus, rather than tuning settings based on intuition.

questions.q: What is the default and generally recommended Optimize tab setting?
options: Use current partitioning — repartitioning itself takes time, so override it only deliberately
Single partition, for simplicity
Round robin, always, regardless of the data
There is no default — a partition type must always be chosen manually
questions.explain: Use current partitioning avoids the real cost of repartitioning and is the right choice in most scenarios — deliberate overrides are for specific, known needs.

questions.q: Why is Single partition strongly discouraged?
options: It combines all distributed data into one partition, which is slow and drags down every downstream step
It's the fastest option, but only works for small datasets
It's only available for SQL Server sources
It automatically disables schema drift
questions.explain: Single partition undoes Spark's distributed processing advantage entirely, significantly slowing the current step and everything downstream of it.

questions.q: What's the tradeoff between the Verbose, Basic, and None logging levels?
options: Verbose logs full per-partition detail (expensive); Basic logs only durations; None gives just a summary — reserve Verbose for active troubleshooting
They are purely cosmetic and have no effect on performance
Basic is the most detailed level, Verbose the least
Logging level only affects the Author hub, not actual run performance
questions.explain: Verbose logging is genuinely expensive to produce. Running it by default on every production run — rather than only when actively troubleshooting — is an avoidable performance cost.
